        type: bind
        source: ./clickhouse-config.xml
        target: /etc/clickhouse-server/config.d/appwrite.xml
        read_only: true
        content: "<?xml version=\"1.0\"?>\n<!--\n    Retention for ClickHouse's own system log tables.\n\n    Every <ttl> in the image's config.xml sits inside an XML comment, so these\n    tables keep every row forever, and the metric ones add a row per second\n    whether or not the instance serves traffic. Left alone they outgrow the\n    usage data they sit next to and fill the volume.\n\n    When a window here changes, ClickHouse replaces the table on the next\n    restart and keeps the old one, rows and all, as <log>_<N>.\n    clickhouse-init.sh gives those old tables the same window.\n-->\n<clickhouse>\n    <!-- The metric, trace and profile logs sample the server every second whether\n         or not Appwrite serves traffic, and nothing reads them back, so their\n         writes and the merges behind them are pure overhead. -->\n    <asynchronous_metric_log remove=\"1\"/>\n    <metric_log remove=\"1\"/>\n    <histogram_metric_log remove=\"1\"/>\n    <query_metric_log remove=\"1\"/>\n    <processors_profile_log remove=\"1\"/>\n    <trace_log remove=\"1\"/>\n    <!-- text_log repeats the server log the container already writes. -->\n    <text_log remove=\"1\"/>\n\n    <!-- Kept for debugging, capped so they cannot fill the volume. -->\n    <asynchronous_insert_log><ttl>event_date + INTERVAL 3 DAY DELETE</ttl></asynchronous_insert_log>\n    <query_log><ttl>event_date + INTERVAL 7 DAY DELETE</ttl></query_log>\n    <query_views_log><ttl>event_date + INTERVAL 7 DAY DELETE</ttl></query_views_log>\n    <query_thread_log><ttl>event_date + INTERVAL 7 DAY DELETE</ttl></query_thread_log>\n    <part_log><ttl>event_date + INTERVAL 7 DAY DELETE</ttl></part_log>\n    <background_schedule_pool_log><ttl>event_date + INTERVAL 7 DAY DELETE</ttl></background_schedule_pool_log>\n\n    <!-- Longer, so it still covers a report that reaches us late. crash_log is\n         deliberately left alone: it is tiny and worth keeping. -->\n    <error_log><ttl>event_date + INTERVAL 14 DAY DELETE</ttl></error_log>\n</clickhouse>\n"
      -
        type: bind
        source: ./clickhouse-init.sh
        target: /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/clickhouse-init.sh
        read_only: true
        content: "#!/bin/bash\n# The ClickHouse entrypoint sources this file, so a subshell keeps these options out of it.\n(\n  set -euo pipefail\n\n  client() {\n    clickhouse-client --host 127.0.0.1 --user \"$CLICKHOUSE_USER\" --password \"$CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD\" \"$@\"\n  }\n\n  # Flushing replaces log tables whose definition changed, keeping each old table as <log>_<N>.\n  client --query 'SYSTEM FLUSH LOGS'\n\n  # Tables left behind never expire on their own: take the TTL of the log that\n  # replaced this one, or a week when the log is no longer written at all.\n  # The named logs must match the ones clickhouse-config.xml removes: a log that\n  # is still written gets replaced on the next restart if its TTL is altered here.\n  client --format TSVRaw <<'SQL' | client --multiquery\nSELECT concat('ALTER TABLE system.', stale.name, ' MODIFY TTL ', if(active.name = '', 'event_date + INTERVAL 7 DAY DELETE', splitByString(' SETTINGS ', splitByString(' TTL ', active.engine_full)[2])[1]), ';')\nFROM (\n  SELECT name, splitByChar('_', name)[-1] AS suffix, arrayStringConcat(arrayPopBack(splitByChar('_', name)), '_') AS log\n  FROM system.tables\n  WHERE database = 'system'\n    AND position(engine_full, ' TTL ') = 0\n    AND endsWith(engine, 'MergeTree')\n    AND name IN (SELECT table FROM system.columns WHERE database = 'system' AND name = 'event_date' AND type = 'Date')\n) AS stale\nLEFT JOIN system.tables AS active\n  ON active.database = 'system'\n  AND active.name = stale.log\n  AND position(active.engine_full, ' TTL ') > 0\nWHERE (endsWith(stale.log, '_log') AND toUInt64OrNull(stale.suffix) IS NOT NULL)\n  OR stale.name IN ('asynchronous_metric_log', 'metric_log', 'histogram_metric_log', 'query_metric_log', 'processors_profile_log', 'trace_log', 'text_log')\nSQL\n)\n"
    ulimits:
      nofile:
        soft: 262144
        hard: 262144
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD-SHELL
        - 'clickhouse-client --user "$$CLICKHOUSE_USER" --password "$$CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD" --query "SELECT 1" > /dev/null || exit 1'
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 20
      start_period: 30s

        content: "<?xml version=\"1.0\"?>\n<!--\n    Retention for ClickHouse's own system log tables.\n\n    Every <ttl> in the image's config.xml sits inside an XML comment, so these\n    tables keep every row forever, and the metric ones add a row per second\n    whether or not the instance serves traffic. Left alone they outgrow the\n    usage data they sit next to and fill the volume.\n\n    When a window here changes, ClickHouse replaces the table on the next\n    restart and keeps the old one, rows and all, as <log>_<N>.\n    clickhouse-init.sh gives those old tables the same window.\n-->\n<clickhouse>\n    <!-- The metric, trace and profile logs sample the server every second whether\n         or not Appwrite serves traffic, and nothing reads them back, so their\n         writes and the merges behind them are pure overhead. -->\n    <asynchronous_metric_log remove=\"1\"/>\n    <metric_log remove=\"1\"/>\n    <histogram_metric_log remove=\"1\"/>\n    <query_metric_log remove=\"1\"/>\n    <processors_profile_log remove=\"1\"/>\n    <trace_log remove=\"1\"/>\n    <!-- text_log repeats the server log the container already writes. -->\n    <text_log remove=\"1\"/>\n\n    <!-- Kept for debugging, capped so they cannot fill the volume. -->\n    <asynchronous_insert_log><ttl>event_date + INTERVAL 3 DAY DELETE</ttl></asynchronous_insert_log>\n    <query_log><ttl>event_date + INTERVAL 7 DAY DELETE</ttl></query_log>\n    <query_views_log><ttl>event_date + INTERVAL 7 DAY DELETE</ttl></query_views_log>\n    <query_thread_log><ttl>event_date + INTERVAL 7 DAY DELETE</ttl></query_thread_log>\n    <part_log><ttl>event_date + INTERVAL 7 DAY DELETE</ttl></part_log>\n    <background_schedule_pool_log><ttl>event_date + INTERVAL 7 DAY DELETE</ttl></background_schedule_pool_log>\n\n    <!-- Longer, so it still covers a report that reaches us late. crash_log is\n         deliberately left alone: it is tiny and worth keeping. -->\n    <error_log><ttl>event_date + INTERVAL 14 DAY DELETE</ttl></error_log>\n</clickhouse>\n"
      -
        type: bind
        source: ./clickhouse-init.sh
        target: /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/clickhouse-init.sh
        read_only: true
        content: "#!/bin/bash\n# The ClickHouse entrypoint sources this file, so a subshell keeps these options out of it.\n(\n  set -euo pipefail\n\n  client() {\n    clickhouse-client --host 127.0.0.1 --user \"$CLICKHOUSE_USER\" --password \"$CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD\" \"$@\"\n  }\n\n  # Flushing replaces log tables whose definition changed, keeping each old table as <log>_<N>.\n  client --query 'SYSTEM FLUSH LOGS'\n\n  # Tables left behind never expire on their own: take the TTL of the log that\n  # replaced this one, or a week when the log is no longer written at all.\n  # The named logs must match the ones clickhouse-config.xml removes: a log that\n  # is still written gets replaced on the next restart if its TTL is altered here.\n  client --format TSVRaw <<'SQL' | client --multiquery\nSELECT concat('ALTER TABLE system.', stale.name, ' MODIFY TTL ', if(active.name = '', 'event_date + INTERVAL 7 DAY DELETE', splitByString(' SETTINGS ', splitByString(' TTL ', active.engine_full)[2])[1]), ';')\nFROM (\n  SELECT name, splitByChar('_', name)[-1] AS suffix, arrayStringConcat(arrayPopBack(splitByChar('_', name)), '_') AS log\n  FROM system.tables\n  WHERE database = 'system'\n    AND position(engine_full, ' TTL ') = 0\n    AND endsWith(engine, 'MergeTree')\n    AND name IN (SELECT table FROM system.columns WHERE database = 'system' AND name = 'event_date' AND type = 'Date')\n) AS stale\nLEFT JOIN system.tables AS active\n  ON active.database = 'system'\n  AND active.name = stale.log\n  AND position(active.engine_full, ' TTL ') > 0\nWHERE (endsWith(stale.log, '_log') AND toUInt64OrNull(stale.suffix) IS NOT NULL)\n  OR stale.name IN ('asynchronous_metric_log', 'metric_log', 'histogram_metric_log', 'query_metric_log', 'processors_profile_log', 'trace_log', 'text_log')\nSQL\n)\n"
    ulimits:
      nofile:
        soft: 262144
        hard: 262144
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD-SHELL

      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 20
      start_period: 30s

file_volumes.content:
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!--
    Retention for ClickHouse's own system log tables.

    Every <ttl> in the image's config.xml sits inside an XML comment, so these
    tables keep every row forever, and the metric ones add a row per second
    whether or not the instance serves traffic. Left alone they outgrow the
    usage data they sit next to and fill the volume.

    When a window here changes, ClickHouse replaces the table on the next
    restart and keeps the old one, rows and all, as <log>_<N>.
    clickhouse-init.sh gives those old tables the same window.
-->
<clickhouse>
    <!-- The metric, trace and profile logs sample the server every second whether
         or not Appwrite serves traffic, and nothing reads them back, so their
         writes and the merges behind them are pure overhead. -->
    <asynchronous_metric_log remove="1"/>
    <metric_log remove="1"/>
    <histogram_metric_log remove="1"/>
    <query_metric_log remove="1"/>
    <processors_profile_log remove="1"/>
    <trace_log remove="1"/>
    <!-- text_log repeats the server log the container already writes. -->
    <text_log remove="1"/>

    <!-- Kept for debugging, capped so they cannot fill the volume. -->
    <asynchronous_insert_log><ttl>event_date + INTERVAL 3 DAY DELETE</ttl></asynchronous_insert_log>
    <query_log><ttl>event_date + INTERVAL 7 DAY DELETE</ttl></query_log>
    <query_views_log><ttl>event_date + INTERVAL 7 DAY DELETE</ttl></query_views_log>
    <query_thread_log><ttl>event_date + INTERVAL 7 DAY DELETE</ttl></query_thread_log>
    <part_log><ttl>event_date + INTERVAL 7 DAY DELETE</ttl></part_log>
    <background_schedule_pool_log><ttl>event_date + INTERVAL 7 DAY DELETE</ttl></background_schedule_pool_log>

    <!-- Longer, so it still covers a report that reaches us late. crash_log is
         deliberately left alone: it is tiny and worth keeping. -->
    <error_log><ttl>event_date + INTERVAL 14 DAY DELETE</ttl></error_log>
</clickhouse>

#!/bin/bash
# The ClickHouse entrypoint sources this file, so a subshell keeps these options out of it.
(
  set -euo pipefail

  client() {
    clickhouse-client --host 127.0.0.1 --user "$CLICKHOUSE_USER" --password "$CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD" "$@"
  }

  # Flushing replaces log tables whose definition changed, keeping each old table as <log>_<N>.
  client --query 'SYSTEM FLUSH LOGS'

  # Tables left behind never expire on their own: take the TTL of the log that
  # replaced this one, or a week when the log is no longer written at all.
  # The named logs must match the ones clickhouse-config.xml removes: a log that
  # is still written gets replaced on the next restart if its TTL is altered here.
  client --format TSVRaw <<'SQL' | client --multiquery
SELECT concat('ALTER TABLE system.', stale.name, ' MODIFY TTL ', if(active.name = '', 'event_date + INTERVAL 7 DAY DELETE', splitByString(' SETTINGS ', splitByString(' TTL ', active.engine_full)[2])[1]), ';')
FROM (
  SELECT name, splitByChar('_', name)[-1] AS suffix, arrayStringConcat(arrayPopBack(splitByChar('_', name)), '_') AS log
  FROM system.tables
  WHERE database = 'system'
    AND position(engine_full, ' TTL ') = 0
    AND endsWith(engine, 'MergeTree')
    AND name IN (SELECT table FROM system.columns WHERE database = 'system' AND name = 'event_date' AND type = 'Date')
) AS stale
LEFT JOIN system.tables AS active
  ON active.database = 'system'
  AND active.name = stale.log
  AND position(active.engine_full, ' TTL ') > 0
WHERE (endsWith(stale.log, '_log') AND toUInt64OrNull(stale.suffix) IS NOT NULL)
  OR stale.name IN ('asynchronous_metric_log', 'metric_log', 'histogram_metric_log', 'query_metric_log', 'processors_profile_log', 'trace_log', 'text_log')
SQL
)

file_volumes.content:
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!--
    Retention for ClickHouse's own system log tables.

    Every <ttl> in the image's config.xml sits inside an XML comment, so these
    tables keep every row forever, and the metric ones add a row per second
    whether or not the instance serves traffic. Left alone they outgrow the
    usage data they sit next to and fill the volume.

    When a window here changes, ClickHouse replaces the table on the next
    restart and keeps the old one, rows and all, as <log>_<N>.
    clickhouse-init.sh gives those old tables the same window.
-->
<clickhouse>
    <!-- The metric, trace and profile logs sample the server every second whether
         or not Appwrite serves traffic, and nothing reads them back, so their
         writes and the merges behind them are pure overhead. -->
    <asynchronous_metric_log remove="1"/>
    <metric_log remove="1"/>
    <histogram_metric_log remove="1"/>
    <query_metric_log remove="1"/>
    <processors_profile_log remove="1"/>
    <trace_log remove="1"/>
    <!-- text_log repeats the server log the container already writes. -->
    <text_log remove="1"/>

    <!-- Kept for debugging, capped so they cannot fill the volume. -->
    <asynchronous_insert_log><ttl>event_date + INTERVAL 3 DAY DELETE</ttl></asynchronous_insert_log>
    <query_log><ttl>event_date + INTERVAL 7 DAY DELETE</ttl></query_log>
    <query_views_log><ttl>event_date + INTERVAL 7 DAY DELETE</ttl></query_views_log>
    <query_thread_log><ttl>event_date + INTERVAL 7 DAY DELETE</ttl></query_thread_log>
    <part_log><ttl>event_date + INTERVAL 7 DAY DELETE</ttl></part_log>
    <background_schedule_pool_log><ttl>event_date + INTERVAL 7 DAY DELETE</ttl></background_schedule_pool_log>

    <!-- Longer, so it still covers a report that reaches us late. crash_log is
         deliberately left alone: it is tiny and worth keeping. -->
    <error_log><ttl>event_date + INTERVAL 14 DAY DELETE</ttl></error_log>
</clickhouse>

#!/bin/bash
# The ClickHouse entrypoint sources this file, so a subshell keeps these options out of it.
(
  set -euo pipefail

  client() {
    clickhouse-client --host 127.0.0.1 --user "$CLICKHOUSE_USER" --password "$CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD" "$@"
  }

  # Flushing replaces log tables whose definition changed, keeping each old table as <log>_<N>.
  client --query 'SYSTEM FLUSH LOGS'

  # Tables left behind never expire on their own: take the TTL of the log that
  # replaced this one, or a week when the log is no longer written at all.
  # The named logs must match the ones clickhouse-config.xml removes: a log that
  # is still written gets replaced on the next restart if its TTL is altered here.
  client --format TSVRaw <<'SQL' | client --multiquery
SELECT concat('ALTER TABLE system.', stale.name, ' MODIFY TTL ', if(active.name = '', 'event_date + INTERVAL 7 DAY DELETE', splitByString(' SETTINGS ', splitByString(' TTL ', active.engine_full)[2])[1]), ';')
FROM (
  SELECT name, splitByChar('_', name)[-1] AS suffix, arrayStringConcat(arrayPopBack(splitByChar('_', name)), '_') AS log
  FROM system.tables
  WHERE database = 'system'
    AND position(engine_full, ' TTL ') = 0
    AND endsWith(engine, 'MergeTree')
    AND name IN (SELECT table FROM system.columns WHERE database = 'system' AND name = 'event_date' AND type = 'Date')
) AS stale
LEFT JOIN system.tables AS active
  ON active.database = 'system'
  AND active.name = stale.log
  AND position(active.engine_full, ' TTL ') > 0
WHERE (endsWith(stale.log, '_log') AND toUInt64OrNull(stale.suffix) IS NOT NULL)
  OR stale.name IN ('asynchronous_metric_log', 'metric_log', 'histogram_metric_log', 'query_metric_log', 'processors_profile_log', 'trace_log', 'text_log')
SQL
)
